sources.shortCitation: “Im Selenophon-Atelier arbeitet Robert Wohlmuth …” — Mein Film, no. 248 (1930)
sources.fullCitation: [Photographs from the production of Bünzlis Abenteuer at the Selenophon studio]. Mein Film (Vienna), no. 248 (1930): 7. Österreichische Nationalbibliothek / ANNO.
sources.title: Robert Wohlmuth and his crew filming Bünzlis Abenteuer — Mein Film, 1930
sources.researchNote: A report from the Selenophon studio on the sound film Bünzlis Abenteuer, directed by Robert Wohlmuth. The caption reads: “Links: Im Selenophon-Atelier arbeitet Robert Wohlmuth und sein Stab fieberhaft an dem Film „Bünzlis Abenteuer“. Obere Reihe: Aufnahmeleiter I. W. Bayer, Kameramann O. Schnürch, Heinrich Bünzli, Regisseur Robert Wohlmuth, Mizzi Gribl, Atelierchef I. Zehetmeier. Zweite Reihe: Tonregisseur Alexander Perfall, Architekt Ledersteger, Aufnahmeleiter I. A. Wesely, Ing. Benda.” It names the upper row in order, and Mizzi Gribl, the only woman in that row, stands fifth in the caption and fifth from the left in the photograph; the man immediately to her left is therefore Wohlmuth. The detail taken from the photograph is small — his head measures about eighty-five pixels across in the scan — and it is a halftone, so it carries the grain of the printed screen. The same page credits the film’s parody score to a Paul Mann, a name the archive also carries for the composer of Heut kommt’s drauf an; nothing here establishes that they are the same man.

media.title: Robert Wohlmuth — portrait, 1930
media.description: Detail of the Selenophon studio photograph printed in Mein Film in 1930, showing the director Robert Wohlmuth. The caption names the upper row in order and places Mizzi Gribl, the only woman in it, fifth; Wohlmuth stands immediately to her left.
media.altText: A young man with dark hair brushed back, in a light open-necked shirt, looking past the camera; a detail of a halftone group photograph.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. Detail of a photograph published in an Austrian film weekly in 1930 with no photographer credited; the Austrian term for a simple photograph expired fifty years after publication.
media.publicCaption: Robert Wohlmuth in 1930, at work on Bünzlis Abenteuer: a detail of the studio photograph printed in Mein Film, no. 248, page 7.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer unidentified; Mein Film, no. 248 (1930): 7, detail. Österreichische Nationalbibliothek / ANNO.
